summary: Backend-only iteration-5 regression + full verification of the Nest Concierge personalization stack and the three polish items (ReDoS-safe search, product-list aggregation with average_rating/review_count, refund-on-cancel). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5_concierge.py with 25 tests across 6 classes: Regression (root, categories, collections, editorials, /auth/me, wishlist toggle, orders create/list, mock-pay), Search-ReDoS (parametrized on 'a(b*)+', '.*(.*)', '(x+)+', '((a+)+)+', '[[[[' — each returns 200 in <5s and JSON list; 'Blush' still hits 'Blush Rose Dinner Set' case-insensitive), Product-List Ratings (every product carries numeric average_rating + int review_count; posting rating=4 and rating=5 by two fresh users on one product produces review_count>=2 and average_rating 3.5-5.0; recursive scan proves NO '_id' and NO '_reviews' anywhere in the payload), Refund-on-Cancel (create order with points redeemed → balance drops by exact redeemed amount → admin PUT /admin/orders/{id}/status status='cancelled' → balance restored to pre-order value, user_points.transactions gains exactly ONE type='earn'/reason='order_refund' tx with meta.order_id=that order, second cancel is idempotent and does NOT re-refund; cancelling a points_redeemed=0 order produces zero refund tx), Interactions (POST requires auth=401, invalid event 'purchase'=400, unknown product_id=400, all five valid events {view,wishlist,review,shortlist_add,cart_add} accepted and stored; response never leaks _id), Recommendations (GET requires auth=401; cold-start returns list<=8 without crashing; after posting 3 'view' interactions on subcategory='cups' the response NEVER contains any of the 3 seen ids AND biases toward dining/cups; limit=3 respected; recursive scan proves no _id leak). Result: 25/25 PASSED in 5.94s.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1222 lines — well beyond the 700-line split threshold. Split into routers/ (auth, products, taxonomy, editorials, shortlists, orders, payments, reviews, points, interactions, recommendations).
Deprecated @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') still in use (server.py:1178, 1219) — migrate to FastAPI lifespan context manager.

Startup still runs destructive db.products.delete_many({}) and db.editorials.delete_many({}) on every restart (server.py:1196, 1213). Any admin-created products/editorials are wiped on `supervisorctl restart backend`.

Recommendations aggregation adds a 'score' field via a suspicious $addFields expression at server.py:788-797 that references Python locals (subs) inside the pipeline — the constant list is captured at pipeline-build time and does not actually vary per-document, so the current 'score' provides no real ranking. Consider using $switch/$in against a $literal map, or drop the field. The endpoint currently succeeds only because it also applies $sample and $project drops 'score'.

Recommendation 'fill' branch requires featured=True products to backfill (server.py:807). If a user has viewed all featured items, the response can end up shorter than 'limit'. Consider also filling with random non-featured products before returning.
Interactions collection has no indexes on (user_id, created_at) — the /recommendations aggregation with $sort+$limit will scan-and-sort as data grows. Add compound index.

InteractionIn.event validation is done manually against ALLOWED_EVENTS at server.py:708 — better modeled as a Literal / enum in Pydantic so 422 (unprocessable) is returned automatically and OpenAPI schema is accurate.
Product-list aggregation performs $lookup on reviews for every request without an index on reviews.product_id — add db.reviews.create_index('product_id') at startup.

Order status transitions are unvalidated — admin can still flip 'delivered' back to 'created'. Refund-on-cancel is guarded by 'was_cancelled' but no other transition guard exists (e.g. cancelling an already-shipped order still triggers a full refund).
Review body/title have no length cap — a user could store multi-MB text. Add max_length to Pydantic ReviewIn.
seed_data_creation: Tests self-create ~8 disposable users per run (TEST_it5_<hex10>@garlicnest.com) with mobiles derived from the same random hex, plus a handful of interactions/orders/reviews/points_txs against the auto-seeded products. Backend restart re-seeds products+editorials (destroying created products) but reviews/orders/interactions/points/wishlists/users persist. No admin delete-user endpoint exists, so TEST_it5_* users accumulate — main agent may consider adding one for cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 polish items and both personalization endpoints verified against the live external ingress (EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL). Key behaviours: (1) GET /api/products?q=<x> now escapes user input via re.escape — safe against regex-metachar payloads. (2) GET /api/products returns each item with numeric average_rating (0.0 default, rounded 1dp when reviews exist) and int review_count via a single $lookup aggregation; '_id' and '_reviews' are stripped in the pipeline's final $project. (3) PUT /api/admin/orders/{id}/status status='cancelled' refunds order.points_redeemed via _award_points(reason='order_refund', meta.order_id=<id>) exactly once — second cancel is a no-op because the code checks was_cancelled = order.get('status')=='cancelled' before refunding. (4) POST /api/interactions {product_id,event} — event must be in {view,cart_add,wishlist,shortlist_add,review}; weights are 1/3/4/5/6 respectively; unknown product_id returns 400; unauthenticated returns 401. (5) GET /api/recommendations?limit=N — auth required; aggregates by subcategory/category/collection affinity with per-event weights; excludes already-seen ids; cold-start users get up to N random featured products; if the personalized branch returns <N, backfills with unseen featured products (never leaking already-seen). Response is _id-free. Test file is fully self-contained and safe to re-run — it derives unique mobile numbers per run and mode-of-operation is idempotent.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no backend bugs found. All 25 assertions pass on first run against the live ingress.
